correctness.rationale: For each n>=4 the complete overlap graph has 2F_(n+1) edges and exactly 2F_(n-3) vertices with outdegree exceeding indegree by one. Every closed edge-simple trail must omit at least one outgoing edge per such vertex. The deleted double-prefix/double-suffix windows balance all degrees; alternating-bit routes prove the remainder strongly connected and thus Eulerian. In an optimum, deleting the other outgoing edge of a positive vertex unbalances a zero-imbalance head, proving equality rigidity. The extracted standalone checker independently reconstructs finite instances n=3..16 and exhaustively verifies n=4,5, complementing the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The one-sided constrained result cannot be used as a sharp bound for the two-sided restriction merely by substitution: our upper-bound obstruction is the imbalance of both endpoint double-pair types, and the unique optimal set is a proper balanced subset of the two-sided admissible graph. The rotation-closed universal-cycle theorem has a hypothesis that the present optimum window set demonstrably fails.

value.rationale: Combining run-length limited transmission and unique cyclic window identification creates a natural constrained cut-down de Bruijn capacity problem. The forced asymmetry of the allowed full overlap graph means naive counts of allowed windows and existing single-symbol RLL universal cycles do not give this capacity. The result solves the exact optimum for every order n>=4 and establishes a rigid common optimum edge set with an Eulerian construction, a substantive structural answer rather than a numerical lookup.
